executive_summary: The supplied files show several label and horizon issues that should be audited before hyperparameter work. The strongest observed issues are: direction_1h is a fixed endpoint-return label rather than a first-touch liquidity-sweep label; training rows are dense overlapping snapshots; calendar/symbol features dominate the 1h direction task; and high event/direction metrics in squeeze backtests do not translate into positive net bps under the reported assumptions. Sweep-label code does implement UPPER_FIRST, LOWER_FIRST, NONE, BOTH and INVALID logic, but downstream treatment of BOTH/INVALID and repeated timestamp independence need explicit measurement. Evidence for the original squeeze-event label builder is incomplete because scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py is referenced but not supplied.

findings.title: direction_1h is an endpoint-return label, not a first-touch topology/liquidity label

evidence.detail: add_forward_labels computes future_price at target_time via merge_asof, forward_return = future_price/current_price - 1.0, and direction = 1/-1/0 using fixed neutral thresholds.
The CatBoost target is direction_1h with classes -1, 0, 1.
A separate first-touch sweep label exists and inspects future prices in (logged_at, logged_at + horizon] against fixed upper/lower liquidity levels.

findings.why_it_matters: If the research problem is liquidation-topology or which liquidity side is swept first, endpoint return at 1h can conflict with first-touch path behavior. A row can hit upper first and still finish down after 1h, or hit neither level but have a non-neutral endpoint return.
findings.verification_test: Join liq_topology_v2_ml_labeled.parquet and liq_topology_v2_sweep_labels.parquet by id. For 1h valid rows, cross-tab direction_1h against sweep_code_1h and measure disagreement rates, e.g. P(direction_1h=1 | UPPER_FIRST), P(direction_1h=-1 | UPPER_FIRST), P(direction_1h=0 | UPPER_FIRST), and the same for LOWER_FIRST/NONE/BOTH.
findings.recommended_change: Treat endpoint direction and first-touch sweep as separate tasks. For topology-driven liquidation research, prioritize sweep-first or barrier outcome labels, then optionally add endpoint-return labels as secondary economic filters.
findings.success_metric: A documented label-alignment table with disagreement rates below a pre-set threshold, for example less than 20% sign conflict between intended first-touch direction and training target on valid rows, or an explicit decision to model them separately.
findings.risk: Optimizing model hyperparameters on direction_1h can improve classification metrics while failing to predict the tradable topology event.

findings.title: UPPER_FIRST, LOWER_FIRST, NONE, BOTH and INVALID are implemented, but BOTH/INVALID handling is not quantified in supplied reports

evidence.detail: Constants define LABEL_INVALID=-9, LABEL_LOWER_FIRST=-1, LABEL_NONE=0, LABEL_UPPER_FIRST=1, LABEL_BOTH=2.
valid_levels requires finite upper/lower levels, upper_levels >= prices, and lower_levels <= prices. Simultaneous upper/lower first-hit offsets are labeled BOTH.
simulate_candidate only accepts sweep_code_1h equal to the required -1 or 1; it does not trade NONE, BOTH, or INVALID.

findings.why_it_matters: BOTH rows can arise from coarse snapshots or jumps across both barriers between observations. Treating BOTH as invalid/ignored versus loss versus ambiguous changes class balance, label noise, and backtest comparability.
findings.verification_test: Compute row counts and percentages of INVALID, NONE, UPPER_FIRST, LOWER_FIRST, BOTH by symbol/timeframe/horizon. For BOTH rows, inspect median inter-snapshot interval and price move size from source to first-hit timestamp.
findings.recommended_change: Publish a sweep-label audit table and choose an explicit policy: exclude BOTH from training, map BOTH to ambiguous/abstain, or simulate conservatively as adverse first depending on strategy.
findings.success_metric: BOTH and INVALID shares are measured and stable by fold; if BOTH exceeds a pre-set tolerance such as 1-2% of valid rows, downstream metrics are reported both with and without BOTH.
findings.risk: Unmeasured ambiguous labels can inflate or depress first-touch model performance and obscure whether errors are model errors or label-resolution artifacts.

findings.title: Dense snapshot labels create overlapping forward windows; event independence is not established

evidence.detail: Every row receives 15m, 1h and 4h forward labels using future target timestamps.
Every valid row receives 1h and 4h sweep labels by scanning future prices inside the horizon.
The 1h model samples 800000 train rows, 300000 validation rows, and 300000 test rows from 2554739 valid labeled rows.
A non_overlapping_sample function exists for t-statistics in the matrix alignment study, but this overlap control is not shown in the core 1h model training metrics.

findings.why_it_matters: Adjacent snapshots can share most of the same future horizon, so rows are not independent. Standard row-level accuracy, AUC, log loss and confidence intervals can overstate effective sample size.
findings.verification_test: For each symbol/timeframe/horizon, bucket rows into non-overlapping horizon buckets and keep one row per bucket. Recompute model metrics and compare against dense-row metrics. Also estimate label autocorrelation at lags 1, 5, 15, 60 snapshots.
findings.recommended_change: Report both dense-row and non-overlapping/event-cluster metrics. For model validation, add grouped or purged splits that prevent overlapping target windows across train/validation/test and within metric calculations.
findings.success_metric: Non-overlapping test balanced accuracy/AUC remains within a pre-specified degradation bound, for example less than 10% relative drop from dense metrics, and effective sample size is reported.
findings.risk: Hyperparameter tuning on dense overlapping rows may select models that exploit serial persistence rather than independent predictive information.

findings.title: Duplicate IDs are checked, but repeated symbol/timeframe timestamps are not shown to be excluded

evidence.detail: validate_input checks duplicated id, null logged_at, and infinite numeric values.
validate_input checks duplicated id, null logged_at, and non-positive current_price.
validate_input checks duplicated id, null logged_at, and non-positive current_price, but no explicit duplicate logged_at per symbol/timeframe check is present.

findings.why_it_matters: Multiple snapshots with different IDs but identical symbol/timeframe/logged_at can create repeated observations with identical or near-identical labels, inflating row counts and reducing independence.
findings.verification_test: Group liq_topology_v2_ml_features.parquet by symbol, timeframe, logged_at and count duplicates. Report duplicate-timestamp row share, duplicate price share, and whether duplicate groups cross train/validation/test boundaries.
findings.recommended_change: Add a validation step that either enforces uniqueness of symbol/timeframe/logged_at or deterministically deduplicates by latest id/source record before labeling.
findings.success_metric: Duplicate symbol/timeframe/logged_at share equals 0 after preprocessing, or duplicate handling is documented and model metrics are unchanged after deduplication within a pre-set tolerance.
findings.risk: Repeated snapshots can make validation scores optimistic and can bias class counts toward periods with higher logging frequency.

findings.title: Calendar and symbol features dominate the 1h direction task; topology-only is weaker than calendar-only on test

evidence.detail: calendar_only test balanced_accuracy is 0.4501181944262669; topology_only test balanced_accuracy is 0.4038438389491346; combined test balanced_accuracy is 0.44096298934188555.
Top combined features are symbol, dow_sin, is_weekend_utc, hour_sin, hour_cos, log1p_lower_total_volume, log1p_upper_total_volume, dow_cos; many topology features have 0.0 importance.
Top CatBoost features include symbol, dow_sin, hour_sin, hour_cos, is_weekend_utc, and dow_cos before most topology variables.

findings.why_it_matters: The current 1h direction label may be more related to time/session and symbol regime than to liquidation topology. Hyperparameter changes will not fix a problem-definition mismatch.
findings.verification_test: Train/evaluate models with: topology-only, calendar-only, symbol-only, price/volatility-only, and topology residualized against calendar/symbol. Evaluate by symbol/timeframe and non-overlapping buckets.
findings.recommended_change: Reframe the label toward topology-specific path events such as first sweep, farther-side sweep, or post-sweep continuation, and report incremental lift of topology features over calendar/symbol baselines.
findings.success_metric: Topology feature block produces positive out-of-sample incremental lift versus calendar/symbol baseline on non-overlapping rows, for example at least +0.02 balanced accuracy or a statistically tested lift in top-decile event rate.
findings.risk: A model may appear predictive by exploiting calendar priors while not learning liquidation topology.

findings.title: Several core labels use fixed time horizons and fixed bps thresholds rather than volatility-normalized horizons

evidence.detail: HORIZONS are fixed at 15m, 1h, 4h; neutral thresholds are fixed at 0.0005, 0.0010, 0.0020.
POST_HIT_WINDOW is fixed at 15 minutes and thresholds are fixed at 10bp and 25bp.
The squeeze research grid includes VOLATILITY_QUANTILES 0.90, 0.95, 0.975, but this volatility-aware concept is not shown in direction_1h labels.

findings.why_it_matters: A fixed 25bp or 1h label can mean different things across BTC, ETH, SOL, gold/silver symbols, timeframes, and volatility regimes. This can create heteroskedastic label noise and unstable class balance.
findings.verification_test: Compute realized volatility or ATR over pre-observation windows and stratify label rates and model metrics by volatility decile. Compare fixed bps labels to sigma-normalized labels and variable time-to-barrier horizons.
findings.recommended_change: Add volatility-normalized target variants: e.g., barrier = k times recent realized volatility, horizon = min fixed time and volatility-clock threshold, or class weights stratified by realized volatility.
findings.success_metric: Class balance and top-decile lift are more stable across volatility deciles; report coefficient of variation of event rate by volatility decile before and after normalization.
findings.risk: Models may learn volatility regime rather than topology, and thresholds may be too easy in high volatility and too rare in low volatility.

findings.title: Direction-confidence thresholds do not change selected top squeeze configurations in supplied reports

evidence.detail: Top configurations 3934-5394 have identical alerts, event_precision, direction_accuracy, trade counts and economic metrics across minimum_direction_confidence values 0.55, 0.60, 0.65 and 0.70 for the same alert percentile/cooldown/execution settings.

Top configurations 2278, 2764, 3250 and 3736 have identical raw_signals, trades and metrics across minimum_direction_confidence values 0.55, 0.60, 0.65 and 0.70 for the same threshold/cooldown/execution settings.

findings.why_it_matters: If an abstention threshold does not alter coverage or quality, it is not acting as a meaningful label-noise or uncertainty filter in the selected region.
findings.verification_test: For all scored OOS rows and generated signals, plot coverage, event rate, direction accuracy, mean net bps, and calibration error by direction_confidence decile and threshold.
findings.recommended_change: Calibrate direction probabilities and choose abstention thresholds from validation based on coverage-quality curves, not a static grid alone. Consider separate edge and direction models if confidence is poorly ranked.
findings.success_metric: Increasing confidence threshold produces a monotonic or at least statistically significant improvement in validation direction accuracy or event-conditioned economic proxy while reporting the coverage tradeoff.
findings.risk: False precision: reported high confidence may not reduce label noise or improve decision quality.

findings.title: High event/direction metrics in squeeze reports do not translate into positive net bps under reported execution assumptions

evidence.detail: Best configuration reports event_precision 0.6944444444444444 and direction_accuracy 0.92, but mean_net_bps is -3.3333093933307953 and profit_factor is 0.79241506507768.
Best configuration reports event_rate 1.0 and event_direction_accuracy 0.9852941176470589, but mean_net_bps is -0.0495200280758433 and profit_factor is 0.9955974240039208.

findings.why_it_matters: The label may detect an event without encoding whether the post-alert path provides enough tradable excursion after costs, stops, delays, and target placement.
findings.verification_test: For each alert, compute conditional MFE/MAE after alert and after entry, stratified by true event class, predicted event class, lead time, and confidence. Compare label-positive versus label-negative economic distributions.
findings.recommended_change: Add an economic label or secondary filter such as post-alert net favorable excursion after costs, target-before-stop, or expected value bucket. Keep event detection separate from execution viability.
findings.success_metric: Validation-selected event-positive/economic-positive rows show materially higher post-cost target-before-stop rate than event-positive/economic-negative rows, measured on non-overlapping OOS alerts.
findings.risk: Optimizing event detection alone can produce alerts that are directionally correct but too late, too noisy, or too small after costs.

findings.title: The pipeline uses event probability and direction confidence, but evidence is insufficient that edge and direction are separately calibrated

evidence.detail: score_frame computes squeeze_probability as 1 - probability_no_event and direction_confidence as max(long_squeeze, short_squeeze)/(long_squeeze + short_squeeze) from one multiclass model.
A separate binary strong_contrarian_25bp_1h model exists and reports top-fraction lift, ROC AUC and PR AUC.
A separate binary target exists for farther liquidity side swept first within 1 hour.

findings.why_it_matters: A multiclass softmax can entangle event/no-event probability with direction. Edge probability may be well ranked while direction among events is poorly calibrated, or vice versa.
findings.verification_test: Evaluate two explicit stages: Stage 1 event/edge model for any relevant event; Stage 2 direction model trained only on event-positive or valid first-touch rows. Compare with the current multiclass model using calibration error, coverage, event AUC/PR AUC, and event-conditioned direction accuracy.
findings.recommended_change: Run a controlled two-stage experiment with out-of-fold probabilities: event model, direction conditional model, and an abstention rule based on both edge and direction confidence.
findings.success_metric: Two-stage validation improves event-conditioned direction accuracy or top-decile event lift at matched alert coverage, and calibration error is lower than the multiclass baseline.
findings.risk: A single multiclass model may produce scores that rank alerts well but give unreliable trade direction or abstention signals.

findings.title: Strong-contrarian economic backtest uses future-derived sweep_code and first_hit_seconds during simulation

evidence.detail: The backtest loads SWEEP_LABEL_PATH columns sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h and passes candidates to simulate_candidate.
simulate_candidate returns None unless sweep_code_1h equals the required farther-side code, then computes expected_hit_time_ns from signal_time_ns + first_hit_seconds_1h.
sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h are generated by inspecting future prices inside the horizon.

findings.why_it_matters: This can be a valid proxy for a conditional stop-entry order only if the live strategy would observe the same trigger and cancel conditions without future knowledge. The supplied code does not prove that equivalence.
findings.verification_test: Reimplement the strong-contrarian backtest using only chronological price snapshots and current levels: place virtual far-side trigger and near-side cancellation at signal time, advance through future prices sequentially, and compare trade set, entry times, trigger_rate and net metrics against the label-column simulator.
findings.recommended_change: For execution backtests, do not read sweep_code_1h or first_hit_seconds_1h as decision inputs. Use them only for offline evaluation, or prove equality to a chronological event-driven simulator.
findings.success_metric: Chronological simulator reproduces at least 99% of label-based trade inclusion/exclusion and entry timestamps within one snapshot interval, or discrepancies are reported and label-based metrics are deprecated.
findings.risk: If not equivalent, future-derived labels can leak trigger information and overstate executable selectivity.

findings.title: The source logic for squeeze_event_dataset and detected_squeeze_events is not supplied

evidence.detail: SOURCE_SCRIPT is scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py and expected outputs include detected_squeeze_events.parquet, squeeze_event_dataset.parquet and walk_forward_predictions.parquet.

The backtest consumes squeeze_event_dataset.parquet and detected_squeeze_events.parquet but the supplied file is truncated before full summary logic and does not define how the original squeeze labels were created.
The experiment name includes tf_1h__future_60m__precursor_5m__q_0p975, but the exact event construction rules are not visible in the supplied files.

findings.why_it_matters: Without the event builder, the audit cannot verify label leakage, precursor offset semantics, volatility quantile calculation, class definitions, overlapping event clustering, or whether target_event is independent of features.
findings.verification_test: Provide scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py and a small reproducible sample. Recompute detected_squeeze_events and squeeze_event_dataset from raw features and compare hashes/counts/class distributions with existing outputs.
findings.recommended_change: Freeze and version the squeeze-event label generator with unit tests for precursor windows, future windows, volatility quantile thresholds, event clustering and class assignment.
findings.success_metric: Rebuild produces identical row counts and deterministic event labels; unit tests cover boundary cases at event_time - precursor, event_time, horizon end, and overlapping events.
findings.risk: Squeeze model metrics and backtests cannot be trusted for research decisions until the label-generation process is auditable.

findings.title: Different labels have very different base rates, requiring task-specific metrics and noise audits

evidence.detail: direction_1h sampled train class counts are -1: 297299, 0: 213773, 1: 288928; test counts are -1: 96920, 0: 102012, 1: 101068.
Farther liquidity side swept first target_counts are 0: 1497177 and 1: 857248.
strong_contrarian_25bp_1h positive_rate is 0.08323730847234463.
Test base_rate varies by fold: 0.102016, 0.090364, and 0.05796.

findings.why_it_matters: Accuracy and balanced accuracy are not interchangeable across endpoint direction, sweep-first, and rare strong-continuation labels. Rare positive labels require PR AUC, lift, calibration, and fold-level base-rate controls.
findings.verification_test: For each label family, report fold-level base rate, positive/negative noise proxies, PR AUC, ROC AUC, calibration error, top-fraction lift and group metrics by symbol/timeframe/volatility decile.
findings.recommended_change: Maintain separate evaluation protocols per label: multiclass balanced metrics for endpoint direction; first-touch accuracy/confusion for sweep labels; PR AUC and top-k lift for rare strong-continuation labels.
findings.success_metric: Each label report includes base-rate-adjusted metrics and fold-level stability; no model is selected on a metric inappropriate for its label prevalence.
findings.risk: A model can look acceptable on accuracy while being unusable for rare-event discovery or economically aligned selection.

missing_evidence: scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py is referenced but not supplied, so exact squeeze-event label construction is unknown.
No supplied report gives sweep_code_1h distribution counts for INVALID, NONE, UPPER_FIRST, LOWER_FIRST and BOTH from the generated parquet.
No supplied artifact shows duplicate symbol/timeframe/logged_at counts or repeated snapshot audit results.
No supplied artifact shows non-overlapping-row model metrics for the core direction_1h, sweep, or strong-contrarian models.
No supplied artifact gives calibration curves or reliability diagrams for squeeze_probability, direction_confidence, or strong_contrarian probabilities.
No supplied artifact shows volatility-decile stratified label distributions or model performance for fixed bps/horizon labels.
top_3_next_actions: Freeze the problem definition by selecting the primary observation unit and label family: endpoint return, first-touch sweep, farther-side sweep, or post-sweep economic continuation; then publish label cross-tabs among direction_1h, sweep_code_1h and strong_contrarian_25bp_1h.

Run a label-independence audit: duplicate timestamp counts, overlapping-window effective sample size, non-overlapping bucket metrics, event clustering, and fold-level base-rate stability by symbol/timeframe/volatility decile.
Replace label-column execution shortcuts with chronological simulators and evaluate a two-stage edge-plus-direction pipeline with calibrated abstention before changing model hyperparameters.
